articleTitle: Solutions of some boundary value problems for a class of constitutive relations for non-linear elastic bodies that is not Green elastic
publicationTitle: Quarterly Journal of Mechanics and Applied Mathematics
abstract: Several boundary value problems are solved for a new class of constitutive equation, where the left Cauchy–Green stretch tensor is given as a non-linear function of the Cauchy stress tensor. Some constitutive inequalities and restrictions are proposed as well.

articleTitle: Asymptotic modelling of the JKR adhesion contact for a thin elastic layer
publicationTitle: Quarterly Journal of Mechanics and Applied Mathematics
abstract: The Johnson–Kendall–Roberts model of frictionless adhesive contact is extended to the case of a thin transversely isotropic elastic layer bonded to a rigid base. The leading-order asymptotic models are obtained for both compressible and incompressible elastic layers. The boundary conditions for the contact pressure approximation on the contour of the contact area have been derived from the boundary-layer solutions, which satisfy the condition that the stress intensity factor of the contact pressure density should have the same value all around the contact area boundary. In the incompressible case, a perturbation solution is obtained for a slightly perturbed circular contact area.

articleTitle: Scattering of water waves by an inclined porous plate submerged in ocean with ice cover
publicationTitle: Quarterly Journal of Mechanics and Applied Mathematics
abstract: In the present article, we have studied the problem of scattering of water waves by a porous plate submerged in the ocean and inclined at an angle to the vertical. The problem is formulated in terms of a hypersingular integral equation of the second kind. The hypersingular integral equation is then solved by a collocation method by representing the unknown function using Tchebychev polynomials. The reflection and transmission coefficients are then obtained and presented graphically. It is observed that porosity of the plate dissipates the wave energy and thereby reduces the reflection and transmission of wave energy. However, it is found that the presence of ice cover reduces the dissipation of energy and also the reflection of wave energy and thereby increases the transmission of wave energy. Also, the increase in angle of inclination of porous plate reduces the energy dissipation as well as the reflection of waves.

articleTitle: Influence of surface effect of the edge of a half-plane on the stress concentration around a nearby nanosized hole of arbitrary shape
publicationTitle: Quarterly Journal of Mechanics and Applied Mathematics
abstract: In the problem of a half-plane containing a nearby nanosized hole, it is customary to assume that the edge of the half-plane is traction free. In the context of nanomechanics, however, the more realistic scenario is to incorporate surface effects not only on the edge of the hole but also on the edge of the half-plane. Our results indicate that the incorporation of surface effects on the edge of the half-plane indeed plays a significant role, in particular as the distance between the hole and the half-plane decreases. In fact, we show that the absence of the corresponding surface effect on the edge of the half-plane induces a significant error in the stress concentration around an arbitrary-shaped hole when the distance between the hole and the edge reaches a critical value. We illustrate our results with a variety of examples including circular, elliptical, triangular and square-shaped holes.

articleTitle: Effective properties of periodic tubular structures
publicationTitle: Quarterly Journal of Mechanics and Applied Mathematics
abstract: A method is described to calculate effective tensor properties of a periodic array of two-phase dielectric tubes embedded in a host matrix. The method uses Weierstrass' quasiperodic functions for representation of the potential that considerably facilitates the problem and allows us to find an exact expression for the effective tensor. For weakly interacting tubes, we obtain Maxwell-like approximation of the effective parameter which is in very good agreement with numerical results in considered examples.

articleTitle: Remarks on explicit strong ellipticity conditions for anisotropic or pre-stressed incompressible solids
publicationTitle: Quarterly Journal of Mechanics and Applied Mathematics
abstract: We present a set of explicit conditions, involving the components of the elastic stiffness tensor, which are necessary and sufficient to ensure the strong ellipticity of an orthorhombic incompressible medium. The derivation is based on the procedure developed by Zee and Sternberg (Arch. Rat. Mech. Anal. 83 (1983)) and, consequently, is also applicable to the case of the homogeneously pre-stressed incompressible isotropic solids. This allows us to reformulate the results by Zee and Sternberg in terms of components of the incremental stiffness tensor. In addition, the resulting conditions are specialised to higher symmetry classes and compared with strong ellipticity conditions for plane strain, commonly used in the literature.

articleTitle: Exact solutions for Hele-Shaw free boundary flows around a flat plate of finite length
publicationTitle: Quarterly Journal of Mechanics and Applied Mathematics
abstract: Exact solutions for the one-phase, zero surface tension Hele-Shaw problem describing the source-driven growth of a blob of viscous fluid around a flat plate of finite length are constructed explicitly. These are stated in the form of conformal maps which parameterise the region occupied by the blob. All stages of the growth of the blob are considered: from when injection begins until after the blob has fully engulfed the plate. In this final stage, the region occupied by the blob is doubly connected and the parameterising map is constructed in terms of automorphic functions. Also considered is the limiting case when the source is at infinity. The results are derived by first applying the Baiocchi transform to the governing equations, and then seeking solutions to the transformed problem in terms of the Schwarz function of the free section of the blob's boundary. A key property of this Schwarz function which enables us to construct these solutions is that it must be purely real along the section of the blob's boundary that is in contact with the plate. To illustrate the results, several examples are computed.

articleTitle: A fundamental model exhibiting non-linear oscillatory dynamics in solid oxide fuel cells—the effects of fuel stream humidification
publicationTitle: Quarterly Journal of Mechanics and Applied Mathematics
abstract: In this article, we address the phenomenon of temporal, self-sustained oscillations for a solid oxide fuel cell which utilises a humidified methane fuel stream. Our objective is to uncover the fundamental mechanisms giving rise to current oscillations that have been observed experimentally. To this end, we develop a model based on the fundamental chemical kinetics and transfer processes which take place within the fuel cell. This leads to a three-dimensional dynamical system, which, under typical operating conditions, is rationally reducible to a planar dynamical system. This planar dynamical system was studied in (Sands et al., Proc. R. Soc. Lond. A 470 (2014)) for the case where the parameter <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\bar c_0 \ll 1}$</tex>, corresponding with a weakly humidified fuel stream. In the present article, the structural dynamics of the planar dynamical system for the case where the parameter <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\bar c_0 =O(1)}$</tex>, which corresponds with a humidified fuel stream, are studied in detail. Self-sustained oscillations are shown to arise through Hopf bifurcations in this planar dynamical system, and the key parameter ranges for the occurrence of such oscillations are identified. Fuel stream humidification is also shown to significantly alter the fuel cell dynamics, leading to hysteresis.

articleTitle: Active cloaking of resonant coated inclusions for waves in membranes and Kirchhoff plates
publicationTitle: Quarterly Journal of Mechanics and Applied Mathematics
abstract: The dynamic response of a coated inclusion is considered in the context of active cloaking. The active cloak is achieved for a coated inclusion in the presence of flexural and membrane waves. In this article, we investigate the design of an active cloak for a coated inclusion in three frequency regimes: the low-frequency range, the intermediate range and the higher frequency range in which scattering resonances occur. In the first of these ranges, we extend previous work, which resulted in a simple mass-compensation design for the monopole scatterer, while in the second and third ranges, a combination of the use of an appropriate coating and the appropriate choice of the amplitudes of the active cloaking sources is necessary. We show that such cloaking can indeed be effective in the region of strong scattering resonances. We give closed form analytic expressions for the required amplitudes of the active cloaking sources in the three frequency regions and provide asymptotic estimates and numerical illustrations.

articleTitle: The large-time development of the solution to an initial-value problem for the generalised burgers’ equation
publicationTitle: Quarterly Journal of Mechanics and Applied Mathematics
abstract: In this article, we consider an initial-value problem for the generalized Burgers’ equation. The normalized Burgers’ equation considered is given bywhere <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-\frac{1}{2} \le \delta \not= 0$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$t$</tex> represent dimensionless distance and time respectively. In particular, we consider the case when the initial data has a discontinuous step, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$u(x,0)= u_{+}$</tex> for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x \ge 0$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$u(x,0)=u_{-}$</tex> for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x<0$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$u_{+}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$u_{-}$</tex> are problem parameters with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$u_{+} \not= u_{-}$</tex>. The method of matched asymptotic coordinate expansions is used to obtain the large-<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$t$</tex> asymptotic structure of the solution to this problem, which exhibits a range of large-<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$t$</tex> attractors depending on the problem parameters. Specifically, the solution of the initial-value problem exhibits the formation of (i) an expansion wave when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\delta>-\frac{1}{2}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$u_{+}>u_{-}$</tex>, (ii) a Taylor shock (hyperbolic tangent) profile when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\delta>-\frac{1}{2}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$u_{+}<u_{-}$</tex> and (iii) the Rudenko–Soluyan similarity solution when <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\delta=-\frac{1}{2}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Spectral study of the Laplace–Beltrami operator arising in the problem of acoustic wave scattering by a quarter-plane
publicationTitle: Quarterly Journal of Mechanics and Applied Mathematics
abstract: The Laplace-Beltrami operator (LBO) on a sphere with a cut arises when considering the problem of wave scattering by a quarter-plane. Recent methods developed for sound-soft (Dirichlet) and sound-hard (Neumann) quarter-planes rely on an a priori knowledge of the spectrum of the LBO. In this article we consider this spectral problem for more general boundary conditions, including Dirichlet, Neumann, real and complex impedance, where the value of the impedance varies like <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\alpha / r, r}$</tex> being the distance from the vertex of the quarter-plane and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex> being constant, and any combination of these. We analyse the corresponding eigenvalues of the LBO, both theoretically and numerically. We show in particular that when the operator stops being self-adjoint, its eigenvalues are complex and are contained within a sector of the complex plane, for which we provide analytical bounds. Moreover, for impedance of small enough modulus <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${|\alpha|}$</tex>, the complex eigenvalues approach the real eigenvalues of the Neumann case.

articleTitle: Analytical solutions for Hele-Shaw moving boundary flows in the presence of a circular cylinder
publicationTitle: Quarterly Journal of Mechanics and Applied Mathematics
abstract: Analytical solutions for the one-phase, zero surface tension Hele-Shaw problem describing the source-driven growth of a blob of viscous fluid in both the exterior and the interior of a circular cylinder are constructed explicitly. These are stated in the form of conformal maps which parameterise the region occupied by the blob. The results are derived by first applying the Baiocchi transform to the governing equations, and then seeking solutions to the transformed problem in terms of the Schwarz function of the free section of the blob's boundary. A pivotal role is played by an auxiliary function which gives the modulus of the parameterising map on the pre-image of this free boundary section. On determining this function, the map is found via the solution of a related Schwarz problem, expressed in an integral form. All stages of the growth of the blob are considered. For the exterior flow, this includes after the blob has fully engulfed the cylinder. During this stage, the region occupied by the blob is doubly connected and the parameterising map is constructed in terms of automorphic functions. Also considered, in the exterior case, is when the source is at infinity. To illustrate the results, several examples are computed. Comparisons are also made with existing numerical results.
